statement.designation: Appointed Board Member, Acalanes Union High School District
paragraphs: I am running for re-election to the Acalanes Union High School District Governing Board. It has been an extraordinary experience continuing my advocacy for students as a current board member. We face many challenges as a district, including an education base grant that is too low, unfunded state mandates, and the place of technology in education. As a board, we have worked together to implement policies that safeguard students, are fiscally responsible, and look toward the future.

My husband and I have lived in Walnut Creek for three decades. Our children attended Walnut Creek schools and graduated from Las Lomas High School. I have deep roots in the AUHSD community, having graduated from Campolindo High School.

In addition to my service on the school board, I have held leadership roles in PTA for more than twenty years. I am currently serving on the Executive Board of the Las Trampas Creek Council of PTAs, which provides support and leadership development to PTA schools within the AUHSD attendance area.

I am a strong proponent for providing students with the mental health resources they need to thrive academically and personally. I prioritize student well-being and will continue to work to ensure all students feel welcome at school. I was honored with the Su Stauffer Friends of Education Award, presented to extraordinary volunteers.
I also served on the Citizens Oversight Committee, ensuring taxpayer dollars are spent wisely.
My experience as a governing board member has given me a clear understanding of the issues we face. I respectfully ask for your vote.
StaceySchweppe4AUHSD.com

A Las Lomas parent. Two decades in public education, starting as a high school teacher. Twice elected to the Walnut Creek Governing Board. I’m running for AUHSD Governing Board — Trustee Area 1 — and would be honored to earn your vote.

In 2018 and 2022, voters elected me to the Walnut Creek School District Governing Board. We improved student outcomes, kept the district financially stable, passed a bond measure to improve school facilities, and built strong partnerships with teachers and staff.

Public education is my passion and profession. My entire career is in K-12 education: a math teacher, a school and district leader in California and across the country, a philanthropy executive, and an advisor to school leaders nationwide. I know how school boards work and how they can work better.

The challenges ahead are real. State funding leaves AUHSD with less money per student than most California districts, forcing hard choices about staff, class sizes, and course offerings. Turnover has been high and great schools depend on recruiting, supporting, and retaining great teachers and leaders. Students in elementary school during the pandemic now are entering high school still catching up. A world reshaped by AI means our schools must move faster than ever to prepare students for an unknown future.

I have a personal stake in getting this right. Both of my children attend Walnut Creek public schools — one at Las Lomas, one at Walnut Creek Intermediate. Walnut Creek deserves a dedicated, experienced voice on the AUHSD board. I’d be grateful to be that voice.
nithiniyengar.org

contests.title: Antioch Unified School District, Trustee Area 5

paragraphs: I am running for the Antioch Unified School Board because every student deserves a safe, supportive, high-quality education. As a father of five with four children in Antioch schools, I know how vital strong public schools are for families and our community.

For 18 years I have worked for the City and County of San Francisco and currently working as a Health Worker with the Department of Public Health. As a member of SEIU Local 1021 and the former Vice President of Organizing for our union, I have dedicated myself to advocating for working families, public education, and healthier communities.

I have also stood with the community to help prevent school closures in Oakland and supported replacing armed police in schools with trained safety staff focused on relationship-building and de-escalation.

In Antioch, I have served on the School District Safety Committee and currently serve on the Community Schools Steering Committee. As a parent of a child in special education, I have fought alongside families and educators to secure needed resources.

If elected, I will focus on community partnerships, improving student achievement, supporting teachers and staff, strengthening school safety, and ensuring every child has the academic, social, and emotional support they need. For more information, please visit our website at www.bdawkinsforantioch.com.

statement.designation: Antioch Unified School District Board Member
paragraphs: For nearly 60 years, I have proudly called Antioch home. It has been my honor to serve our community as Mayor, City Councilmember, School Board Trustee, and lifelong advocate for children and families.

I am grateful to have been recognized as a Contra Costa County Women’s Commission Woman of the Year and to have received the City of Antioch’s Lifetime Achievement Award. One of my greatest honors is having the YMCA dedicate its Antioch Child Development Center in my name.

Today, Antioch Unified School District faces important challenges, including maintaining fiscal responsibility, strengthening support for Special Education and English Language Learners, and ensuring safe, positive learning environments on every campus.

My experience in developing balanced budgets and making responsible financial decisions will help ensure that district resources are used effectively to meet the needs of all students while protecting the district’s long-term financial stability.

California’s Local Control Accountability Plan (LCAP) provides funding to support student success, particularly for underserved learners. Strong communication with parents and families is essential, and every decision should be guided by what is best for students.
I remain committed to transparency, accountability, academic excellence, and working collaboratively with families, staff, and the community to prepare every student for a successful future.
I respectfully ask for your support.
Please contact me at [email removed]

contests.title: Brentwood Union School District

paragraphs: Our schools are at a turning point. We have a real opportunity to bring in stronger leadership, fresh ideas, and a clear focus on students and academics. Transparency and fiscal responsibility are essential. I am not a career politician — I am an immigrant, a mother of four school-aged children, and a business owner. I understand that parents want the best education for their children, and teachers work hard to provide it. I am stepping forward to keep our schools strong, competitive, and focused on academics and student success.

School funding depends on student attendance. When enrollment declines, resources shrink and teachers are often the first to feel the impact. We must maintain high standards, safe campuses, and strong academic programs while putting students first — the rest will follow.

As a Board member, I will fight for practical budget strategies that protect classrooms: prioritize teachers and instructional support over administrative growth, align staffing with enrollment, demand full transparency, pursue grants and partnerships, and redirect savings back into academics and teacher retention.

Each student and their parents should know that I am here for them, I hear them, and I will do everything I can to ensure their education, safety, and rights are my priority. I will tell the truth, listen to parents and teachers. I ask for your vote. Let’s choose strong schools and a stronger future — together. Visit [email removed].

My wife and I purchased a home in Brentwood in 2001. Our daughter received her K-12 education in the Brentwood school district. Her schooling was overall a great experience. Our daughter and her husband recently purchased their first home, and I anticipate their children would be attending Brentwood schools. My concern: “Will my grandchildren receive the same quality education my daughter received?” My goal is to help make BUSD better ‘year over year’ with measurable results!

If elected — my goal is: To ensure that ‘age appropriate’ content is being taught in the classroom (allowing parents to opt-out if needed); School board members should review the classroom curriculum before they approve it; Seek feedback from parents regarding the school district’s policies; Understand budgets and subsequent impact; Facilitate discussions with our teachers in order that we can get ahead of issues before they become critical. We need to start here and ‘ground’ ourselves with what really matters for our current and future generations of K-8th students.

In April 2026, I concluded my 42-year career in IT (the last 18 years at Kaiser Permanente). As a career problem solver, I assess issues to gain complete understanding of the situation. By identifying the best solution, I work (hands-on) with teams towards completion. This would be my approach within BUSD. There is too much at stake… I am not willing to gamble with my grandchildren’s or any child’s education!

contests.title: Contra Costa Community College District, Ward 1

paragraphs: Community college opened the door for my family. I’m Dr. Raquel Donoso, a Richmond parent and education leader, running for Trustee of the Contra Costa Community College District to keep that door open for every family. My mother went to community college to become a nurse, changing my family’s trajectory. As a young single mother, I saw firsthand how education creates opportunity when no path exists. Those experiences shaped my life and commitment to public service.

For 20 years, I’ve worked to expand educational opportunities for first-generation students, working adults, and students for whom one setback can mean never coming back. I’ve managed education investments, collaborated with schools and organizations, and know how to turn limited resources into results. Our community colleges change lives. I’ll help more students complete their education and turn their credentials into high-paying careers.

This moment demands experienced leadership. With uncertain funding and rising student needs, every public dollar must be invested wisely. I’ll hold the college district accountable for taxpayer dollars, strengthen partnerships with employers and labor unions, and keep students at the center of every decision. I’m honored to have earned the endorsements of State Senator Jesse Arreguín, Supervisor John Gioia, and Trustee John Marquez. For more: www.raqueldonoso.com

Challenging times demand strong leadership! Funding cuts are worsening with the federal administration’s dismantling of the U.S. Department of Education. Tuition has skyrocketed at UC/State college systems.

As a West County native and alumnus of Contra Costa and Diablo Valley community colleges, I’ll bring my experience as a former Mayor, Vice Mayor, current Councilmember, and statewide legislative advocate for local youth and families to the Contra Costa Community College District Governing Board.

I’m passionate about democratizing access to education. No matter what your age, background, or where you come from, we should all be entitled to an affordable college education. I’ll bring a fresh, hands-on approach so all of us — veterans, re-entry adults, and low-income students can access the skilled trades and Firefighter, Nursing and Paramedic training our colleges provide.

There’s never been a more important time to protect diversity, equity, and inclusion in our community colleges. I’ll protect our affordable academic and career pathways so students don’t incur thousands of dollars in debt — and prioritize addressing student food insecurity and affordable housing challenges for our faculty.

My broad coalition includes Contra Costa County District Office of Education President Sarah Butler, Contra Costa Community College District Trustees Nicholas Bonasera and Andy Li, West Contra Costa Unified School District Trustee Jamela Smith-Folds, District Attorney Diana Becton, East Bay Regional Park District Director Elizabeth Echols, Educators, Labor, Students, Community. Join us!
CameronSasai.com

statement.designation: Contra Costa Community College District, Governing Board Member, Ward 3
paragraphs: When you first elected me, I got to work ensuring our students can afford a quality education that prepares them for four-year college and careers.

Together we have expanded our free tuition program to cover the first two years of college and strengthened direct student support, including no-cost digital textbooks, student housing assistance, and campus childcare. I have also partnered with employers, trades, and educators to strengthen career technical programs.
That’s why I’m the trusted choice of our district’s professors and local education leaders, including County Superintendent Lynn Mackey and Congressman Mark DeSaulnier.

As a Concord High, DVC, and UC graduate, and a former leader in California’s Department of Education, I deeply understand the critical role our community colleges play in our education system and local economy. For our students to succeed, we need to expand vocational programs and recruit the best educators, so all students are prepared for good careers.

With your support, we’ll offer students an even more affordable, world-class education. I’m honored to have the support of State Senator Grayson, Supervisors Ken Carlson and Shanelle Scales-Preston, and our Concord, Martinez, and Pleasant Hill leaders. I hope to earn your support.
RebeccaBarrett.org | (925) 269-7208

contests.title: Contra Costa County Board Of Education, Area 2

paragraphs: Contra Costa County has been our family home for over 40 years. We raised our four children here who graduated from local public schools through college graduation. I want every child in Contra Costa County to have that same opportunity.

My husband and I own a small business, so we understand the value of hard work, accountability, and long-term commitment to community. This community has benefitted our family so much, and I am determined to continue giving back.

My mother was a high school teacher who instilled in me a deep respect for education and public service. That foundation guided me to earn a degree in economics and a Master of Business Administration. Combined with eight years of service as a trustee in the Orinda Union School District, I am prepared to contribute meaningfully to the county level.

As a school board trustee, one of my most rewarding roles was working alongside representatives from multiple school districts to strengthen collaboration and support for students and families. I also valued attending the California School Boards Association Annual Education Conferences. Those experiences reinforced the power of continuous learning and partnership to improve our schools.

My goal on the County Board of Education will be to help ensure that every student receives an excellent education, and a chance to reach their highest potential. I will bring a collaborative, results-focused approach to building strong schools and communities where every child can succeed.
I’d be honored to earn your vote on November 3.

statement.designation: Governing Board Member, Contra Costa County Board of Education, Area 2
paragraphs: I am honored that my fellow trustees recently elected me President of the Contra Costa County Board of Education for 2026. Since first being elected to the County Board in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, I have worked to strengthen oversight, increase transparency, and ensure county programs effectively serve students, especially those most in need.
I’m proud to have earned the endorsement of classroom teachers, education staff, school board members, and educational leaders from across the county, and their encouragement to seek re-election.

During my time on the County Board, I have championed the focus on literacy and improved accountability in alternative education programs, strengthened school safety, and worked collaboratively to promote responsible budgeting and better student outcomes across our county.

As a former Orinda Union School Board member and active school parent, I served on School Site Councils, the Acalanes Budget Committee, and as co-chair of the Las Trampas Creek Council PTA Legislative Team. These experiences have given me practical understanding of how board decisions impact students, families, and educators.

Looking ahead, I will continue to prioritize safe and supportive schools, access to high-quality academics, and career pathways for every student. Currently, I serve as the 2nd VP of Legislation for the Contra Costa County School Boards Association and remain committed to transparency, fiscal responsibility, and ensuring every voice is heard.
I respectfully ask for your vote so we can continue building stronger schools that support every student and prepare the next generation for success.
Learn more: www.sarah-butler.org

paragraphs: I have strived for Spiritual, Social, Mental, Physical and Financial excellence all of my life.
I have a Masters of Divinity Degree to be a priest and am embarrassingly financially successful. I was third in the Olympic Trials in the Northwest in wrestling.
I would like to enable excellence at the J.S.U.S.D.

I have taken my grandchildren to Jujitsu. They teach them exercises and holds, but do not teach them the point system. There is no carrot in front of the horse. No motivation. I would like to incorporate directly applicable knowledge for the students at J.S.U.S.D into the curriculum. This would include the benefits of stock investment and real estate leverage in the Math courses, along with basic plumbing, electric, medical, and carpentry calculations. Essentially incorporating real life reasons for learning in the curriculum. This would include the principals of investing by Warren Buffet and Peter Lynch into the math curriculum, along with PE and PEG ratios. This is simple 5th grade math. It is life changing learning, useful to every student .

There is also no idea of how much a painter makes versus an investment banker. Investment bankers can make several million dollars per year. There should be some basic knowledge of the income of various professions and the demand for the same.
I would like to enable excellence and happiness at the J.S.U.S.D.
I am proud to be a candidate for the John Swett Unified School District School Board because I believe our schools are strongest when students, families, educators, and the community work together.

As the parent of children attending John Swett Unified schools, I understand the hopes and concerns families have for their children’s education. My commitment to our district is rooted in both personal experience and professional service. I was honored to serve on the inaugural Community Schools Action Team, where I collaborated with educators and community partners to strengthen supports for students and families. As a former PTA President, I worked alongside parents, teachers, and administrators to build school spirit, increase family engagement, and advocate for student success.

Professionally, I began my career as a preschool teacher and now serve as a mental health professional, supporting children and families throughout our community. Every day, I see the importance of strong relationships, early intervention, and creating safe, inclusive learning environments where every child can thrive.

If elected, I will be a thoughtful, collaborative leader who listens, values transparency, and makes decisions with students at the center. I am committed to supporting our educators, strengthening partnerships with families, and ensuring every student has the opportunity to succeed.
Together, we can continue building strong schools, supporting strong families, and creating a bright future for every child in John Swett Unified School District.

My name is Teresa Burk and I am running for re-election to the John Swett Unified School Board. It has been such a privilege to serve on the school board for the last four years and I would be honored to continue. During my first term, I maintained a student centered approach to decision making while encouraging greater transparency to fiscally responsible decisions. While educational funding continues to be reduced, I strongly believe in staff, student, and community input on how we spend that funding.

As a retiree of John Swett Unified and a parent to two John Swett graduates, I believe I bring a great deal of experience and positive relationships with our teachers, staff and community from my many different roles within the school district. As a board member, I will work very hard to ensure all students are provided with a safe, equitable, quality education that prepares them for their future, whether that be a four year college, community college, a trades program or the workforce.

paragraphs: As a Knightsen Elementary School District parent, electrical engineer, and Senior Chief in the United States Navy Reserve, I have dedicated my career to service, leadership, and solving challenges. I am running for the Knightsen Elementary School District Board to ensure every student has the opportunity to succeed in a supportive learning environment.

My priorities are to strengthen student learning by expanding STEM education and equipping students with problem-solving skills for future success. I will advocate for well-maintained schools that foster a positive learning environment and support student achievement.
I believe our teachers are the foundation of student success. They deserve the instructional materials, resources, and administrative support necessary to provide the highest quality education.

Knightsen’s proud history and close-knit, small-town character are among our greatest strengths. I am committed to preserving the values that make our community special while ensuring our schools are prepared for the future. As a board member, I will work collaboratively with families and educators to make fiscally responsible decisions, promote transparency and accountability, and ensure the best interests of our students are at the center of every decision.

paragraphs: Current President of the Liberty Union High School District Board of Education, I respectfully ask for your vote to continue the work we’ve begun for our students, families and schools.

longtime Discovery Bay resident, mother of five Liberty Union High School graduates, and a parent in our district for more than 15 years, I understand firsthand the hopes families have for their children’s future. I believe every student deserves a safe, welcoming learning environment, exceptional teachers, and opportunities to succeed–whether their path leads to college, career technical education, military service, or the workforce.

Our board focused on delivering meaningful results while being responsible stewards of taxpayer dollars. Together, we improved student achievement in Math, English and Science; increased the graduation rate; expanded dual enrollment opportunities serving more than 1,200 students each year; strengthened Career Technical Education pathways, invested in safer and more modern campuses; expanded support for students with special needs; and improved communication with families.

I’m proud of the progress, but there’s more work ahead. I remain committed to thoughtful leadership, transparency, fiscal responsibility and working collaboratively with families, educators and our community ensuring every student is prepared for success.
Experienced Leadership. Proven Results. Students First.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
www.electWeber2026.com

My 37 years as a teacher and mentor in the LUHSD district, 10 years as LEA union president, and proud parent of Heritage graduates uniquely qualify me to represent all stakeholders on the Liberty Union High School District Governing Board.

After earning my English degree and credential at UC Davis, I taught all levels of Liberty and Heritage students, from English Language Learners to AP Literature, was LUHSD Teacher of the Year, class advisor, student travel chaperone, and technical director for Heritage High School theatre.

I served as department chair, mentored student teachers, and coached new and experienced teachers as a consulting teacher for LUHSD’s Beginning Teacher Support and Assessment and Peer Assistance and Review programs.
As union president, I worked collaboratively with administration, ensuring safe, equitable working conditions and fiscally responsible contracts to attract and retain qualified educators.
I live in Discovery Bay with my husband, our children attended local K-12 schools, and graduated from UCBerkeley and Cal Poly SLO, thanks to excellent schools and educators.

Now retired, I want to help LUHSD provide academically appropriate and financially sound programs offering all students educational opportunities and socio-emotional support to prepare them for college, careers, and future independence.
Thank you for your consideration.

My connection to MDUSD is personal. I’m a 27-year resident of our community, a parent of four College Park High School graduates, a Veteran, a swim coach, and a Family Support Specialist.

As an active member of district school committees, PTAs, and as a student advocate, I’ve worked alongside teachers, staff, and families to support student programs, and make sure family voices are heard. This work has convinced me that strong schools are built on collaboration, respect, and a shared focus on students.

Our district must make responsible budget decisions while protecting classroom learning and the people who make our schools work. This means recruiting and retaining excellent educators and supporting student mental health, maintaining safe campuses, and expanding access to academics, arts, athletics, and career technical programs.

As an experienced leader and youth coach, I’ve witnessed how teamwork, discipline, belonging, and encouragement help our youth grow in confidence and resilience. Those same values should guide our school district. Every student should be known, challenged, supported, and given the opportunity to discover their strengths.

If elected, I will bring practical experience, a collaborative approach, and a commitment to listening – advocating for transparent government, sound fiscal managernent, and equitable opportunities for every student in Area 2 and across the district.
Vote For

contests.title: Mt. Diablo Unified School District, Trustee Area 4

paragraphs: Our district doesn’t have an exemplary record. Less than half the students can read or do math at grade level. During the last decade these test scores have gradually gotten worse. I’m deeply concerned about these statistics and the lack of initiative towards fixing them. I’m Al Anderson, a husband, father, and lifelong resident of the county. It’s been many years since I worked as a high school teacher, but I have an active teaching credential and have substituted in MDUSD. While a vote for me probably won’t solve all the district’s problems, I’m not content with the status quo and will do my best. Here’s some concerns:

Financial: Our district overspends every year. With no changes, our savings will run out. Respect: Parents are the sole guardians of their children and their concerns should be treated with respect. Conversely, it is essential that teachers be shown respect in the classroom. One disruptive student can hurt an entire class. I favor detentions and suspensions, so teachers can teach and not be zookeepers. Phones: I favor a total ban. Phonics: This should’ve been required long ago. I support following the example of successful districts around the country and holding back third-graders who can’t read near grade level. Social Justice: Let’s ensure the kids can read and think critically before we wade into the mire of political activism.
During the 26 years I’ve lived in Area 4, I’ve also been a soccer coach, scout leader, and community theater director. See www.anderson4mdusd.org.
MDUSD faces real challenges – no one who is paying attention would say otherwise. We’re making measurable progress, and I want to keep building on it, not tear it down or turn back the clock.

My understanding of MDUSD isn’t theoretical – it is real world experience. I’ve coached, been in the classroom, volunteered, and served two terms on the MDUSD Board from 2012 to 2020, including as Board President.
It is important to have a parent’s perspective. I’m the only Board member with a current MDUSD student and all four of my kids attended MDUSD schools.

I hadn’t planned to return to the Board. But when a vacancy opened up last year, community members asked me to step forward – and I said yes, because I’m deeply committed to the success of this District.
I want to continue building on what we have accomplished together:

Improved academic outcomes districtwide, with proficiency up 3% and continued gains projected this year. Reached fair agreements with our teachers and staff to attract and retain outstanding educators. Refinanced bond measures, saving taxpayers millions. Strengthened fiscal oversight to keep MDUSD sound and accountable. Increased college readiness and expanded vocational offerings to make sure every graduate has a bright future. Expanded parent communication and engagement.
I’m proud to have the support of Congressman DeSaulnier, City Council members from Clayton, Concord and Walnut Creek and bipartisan leaders throughout the District.
MDUSD deserves a Board member who is invested in forward progress. I’d be honored to earn your vote.

paragraphs: Leadership isn’t about settling for good enough; it’s about leaving our schools stronger than we found them.

For the past five years, I have had the privilege of serving as an Oakley Union Elementary School District Trustee. As a special education teacher and father with children attending Oakley schools, every decision I make is personal. I want every student–including my own–to have the opportunity to succeed.

As a trustee, I believe our role is to set the vision, establish high expectations, and ensure accountability. I was proud to make Dual Language Immersion a priority for our district, leading to the launch of the program in 2025, and to support the direction that led to our award-winning Teacher Residency Program, helping attract and retain outstanding educators.

While I am proud of what we have accomplished together, our work is not finished. I remain committed to responsible budgeting, transparency, safe and modern schools, and improving student achievement. I believe our students deserve a district that never settles for good enough and always strives to be among the best elementary school districts in the state.
I respectfully ask for your vote so we can continue building stronger schools together
Safety. Community. Commitment. Integrity. Success.

My promise to Oakley… My name is Isaiah Mateas and I am running for the Oakley Union Elementary School Board of Education, Area 4 seat, because I want to serve the community I’ve been a part of all of my life. As a teacher, I know firsthand how the decisions of the Board affect our students, teachers, and school community. I am who you want to stick up for students’ rights. I am who you want to back teachers. I am a School Board member for the community, not for a resumé title.

From over nine years of educating in various spaces, from public schools to juvenile detention centers, I have seen how education impacts our community and shapes our children’s future. The world is changing quicker than we think, and OUESD needs leadership that’s ready for today’s educational challenges. I plan to maintain the excellence Oakley upholds while (1) expanding child safety nets, (2) strengthening student success through our robust Special Education programs and outreach to diverse communities, (3) fighting for teacher compensation, and (4) expanding arts education opportunities. A vote for me is a vote for your child’s future. Full stop.

paragraphs: Our family chose Orinda because we believe in public education and this remarkable community that supports it. Through volunteering in our children’s schools and currently serving as Co-President of the Wagner Ranch Parents’ Club, I’ve seen firsthand what families, teachers, staff, and volunteers can accomplish when we work together.
I’m running for the school board because I believe thoughtful, long-term leadership is essential to preserving what makes Orinda’s schools exceptional.

My professional career leading large organizations taught me the importance of strategic planning, responsible financial stewardship, and making decisions with transparency and integrity. Those principles will guide my decisions as a board member.

As a board member, I’ll focus on putting students first, strengthening communication and partnership with families, supporting our educators, and making long-term decisions that preserve the excellence of Orinda’s schools for future generations.

Our district’s greatest strength is the partnership between our schools and our community. My goal is to build on that foundation through thoughtful leadership, open communication, and a commitment to the families and students we serve.
I respectfully ask for your vote. To learn more, visit VoteJCforOUSD.org.

Public schools are essential to a thriving Orinda. As a mother of three (grades 12th, 8th, and 2nd), longtime school volunteer, and dedicated community advocate, I’ve built my career around supporting children and civic engagement, work that reflects both my professional commitment and personal investment in our community.

I’m running for re-election to the Orinda School District Governing Board to sustain the quality of our curriculum and schools, equipping students and parents with educational excellence. My priorities include strengthening curriculum, fostering a safe school environment that prioritizes mental health and social-emotional wellbeing, improving staff recruitment and retention, and advocating for a responsible budget. These efforts are vital to keeping Orinda a model of educational excellence.

My volunteer work in Orinda schools spans many roles: field trip driver at Del Rey Elementary, Girl Scout Troop Leader, library volunteer at Wagner Ranch Elementary, and board member of the Parents’ Club of OIS. Since being elected to the OUSD Board of Trustees in 2022, I’ve served as both board president and vice president.

Orinda needs leaders willing to tackle the challenges facing our children, families, educators, staff, and administration directly. Together, we can move OUSD forward and deliver results that matter to our students and community.

I’m honored to be endorsed by Assemblymember Rebecca Bauer-Kahan (D-Orinda, OUSD mom), along with many parents, teachers, staff, and administrators throughout Orinda. It would be my privilege to serve another four years, working to secure the brightest possible future for our children.

It has been a privilege to serve on the Orinda School Board for the past four years, and I am seeking reelection in order to continue to guide the positive progress of the District. Our schools are the foundation of the community. It is imperative to maintain the standard of excellence our city expects and to tirelessly strive to improve. I am eager to continue serving, and I have the experience and perspective to lead for another term.

During my tenure, I have remained focused on academic excellence and high-quality programming, fiscal responsibility and developing excellent teachers and staff. I am a pragmatic leader, setting high expectations and working towards improvement. My broader experience in education makes me particularly qualified. I have proudly worked as a California public school teacher and administrator. I am an experienced board member, having previously served on the boards of both a public school district and a private school. I also hold an Ed.M. in education policy and management. As a parent, I have volunteered in our schools and community in numerous capacities.

I will continue to work tirelessly on behalf of all constituents. I will keep students’ needs at the forefront, and I am committed to supporting rigorous and relevant curriculum and programming. Our teachers are at the core of our schools, and I will focus on supporting excellent educators. The school funding model is complicated. I will deploy resources carefully while advocating for adequate funding. I humbly ask for your vote.

Emphasizing academics, the arts, and social-emotional learning prepares students to become responsible citizens with meaningful opportunities. Achieving this requires flexible, responsive, and inclusive learning environments, as outlined in SRVUSD’s Strategic Directions, which I helped develop.

Electing trustees with proven leadership, experience, problem-solving skills, and compassion is essential to strong public schools. For the past 20 years, I have listened to our community, earned constituents’ trust, and helped strengthen education in SRVUSD. Today, more than ever, we need leaders with a proven record of collaborative, respectful leadership. My experience gives me the perspective to balance long-term district priorities with local solutions that serve all students.

My husband, Alec, and I have lived in San Ramon for 29 years, and our three children attended SRVUSD schools. Through service with District, PTA, and community committees, the California School Boards Association, Rotary, and Decoding Dyslexia CA, I remain closely connected to the concerns of parents, students, staff, and the community.
I am the Executive Director and a graduate of Leadership San Ramon Valley, an adult leadership development and community engagement program. Learn more about me at www.rachelhurdforSRVUSD.com.

contests.title: Walnut Creek School District

paragraphs: As the daughter of a retired public school teacher and the parent of Walnut Creek public school students, I know the impact strong public schools have on our children, families, and community. That commitment led me to serve on the Board of the Walnut Creek Education Foundation for ten years, including four years as President. I bring a Master of Science in Marketing from Santa Clara University and experience in school finance, nonprofit governance, and building partnerships that strengthen our schools.

Working with volunteers, educators, district leaders, and community partners, we increased WCEF’s annual fundraising from $850,000 to more than $1.6 million. Those investments helped fund year-long elementary art, music, and science instruction and expanded elective opportunities at Walnut Creek Intermediate and Tice Creek. As President, I advocated for expanding orchestra to our elementary schools and adding additional semester-long electives at Walnut Creek Intermediate.

I am excited to bring this experience to the Walnut Creek School District Board of Education. Our district, like many across California, faces ongoing financial pressures. If elected, I will work to strengthen our long-term fiscal stability while protecting the educational opportunities that define Walnut Creek public schools. I will advocate for additional local and state funding and approach every decision with transparency, collaboration, and a focus on what is best for students. I believe our strongest schools are built when parents, educators, district leaders, local businesses, and community members work together with a shared commitment to helping every student thrive.

The best decisions for our schools come from people who show up: on campus, in classrooms, and talking directly with teachers, staff, and families. That’s true whether you have children in school today, raised kids here years ago, or simply believe strong public schools make Walnut Creek thrive.

I’m not a career politician. I’m a mom of two in the district, an MBA graduate, and a longtime classroom volunteer and PTA leader. My work in communications reinforces the same principle I live by as a parent: good decisions start with listening.

Here’s what I’ve learned: the best insight into our schools already lives inside them. Teachers, staff, and families see what’s working and what isn’t every day. Too often, board decisions rely on secondhand information rather than campus visits and direct conversations with the people doing the work. When those voices aren’t heard, trust erodes. And public trust is what keeps our schools strong for every generation in this community.

I want to change that. I’ll regularly visit every campus, build relationships with teachers and staff, and create meaningful opportunities for families to weigh in before decisions are made. That same approach applies to taxpayer dollars. Accountability means understanding how resources serve students, not just approving what’s on paper. Strong public schools benefit everyone, not just families with kids enrolled today.
With a new superintendent leading our district, this is an exciting moment for WCSD – and the right time for a board that shows up, listens, and builds trust.
Common Sense for Our Schools
I’ve spent a career solving hard problems under pressure, balancing budgets, and bringing people together — now I’m bringing that same discipline to the Walnut Creek School Board.

As a journalist, I learned to stay calm and focus on facts. In health technology, I managed full P&Ls and delivered results without waste. I watched doctors forced to see too many patients with too few resources. Providers burned out. Patients suffered.

Today I see the same pattern in education, with overloaded teachers and students who pay the price. I now use my health policy background to expand access to care, including Medicare and Medi-Cal services that help older adults and people with disabilities stay healthy and independent.

My approach is simple: I listen to the people doing the work, focus on root causes, protect the student-teacher relationship, and strengthen family connections — including grandparents and caregivers — that fight isolation and give kids wisdom and stability. And I keep a sharp eye on costs so every tax dollar delivers results.
If elected, I will apply this same discipline: careful stewardship of tax dollars, clear information for residents, and practical policies that protect our schools, home values, and community.

I am a parent of two children at Indian Valley Elementary, where I volunteer in the classroom. I also serve at our local food bank. I believe in staying close to the work and serving every student, family, caregiver, and resident.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
Read more at www.GGforBoard.com

School gives us our first glimpse of what the world looks like and shows us our place in society. The quality of our education and community shapes not only who we are, but who we think we can become. I am proud to have served the Walnut Creek School District for the last eight years on the Governing Board and I am asking for your support to continue in this role.

The board is responsible to ensure that our families and community experience schools as safe and welcoming environments where every opportunity is available so all our students can reach their fullest potential.

During my tenure, the district completed Measure D construction projects on time and on budget, and is midway through our Measure J projects that will bring our elementary campuses to the same modern standards of our middle schools. Our focus on careful planning and fiscal responsibility has allowed these projects to flourish in parallel with rising student achievement and a comprehensive wellness program that is a model for school districts across the county and the state.

Our community of students, teachers, staff and families continue to face new challenges and are constantly learning and adapting. I have worked to ensure that the board’s decision-making is student-centered with equity and belonging at the heart of our work. I will support our new superintendent to build upon WCSD’s strengths and look ahead to the future.
Thank you for your time and consideration of my candidacy.

Walnut Creek schools have been an important part of my family’s life. As the father of three daughters who have attended Walnut Creek School District schools—with one daughter still enrolled — I understand how deeply every decision made by the Board affects students, families, teachers, and our community.

I am running because I believe every child deserves the opportunity to learn, every teacher deserves our support and respect, and every parent deserves to be heard. Strong schools are built on trust, transparency, collaboration, and a shared commitment to student success.

For more than 25 years, I have led organizations by bringing people together, solving complex problems, and ensuring accountability. As a CPA, business executive, current associate board member of a credit union, and former Co-Vice President of Fundraising for the Tice Creek PTA, I helped raise more than $50,000 to support our schools because investing in our children is one of the greatest investments we can make.

If elected, I will listen with an open mind, communicate honestly, make thoughtful and responsible decisions, and always put students first. My goal is to help strengthen the partnership between families, educators, and the Board so that together we can provide every child with the education and opportunities they deserve.
It would be an honor to earn your trust and your vote.

paragraphs: As a lifelong resident of Antioch, I’ve spent more than 20 years in public service working to make our community safer, stronger, and more connected. I previously served on the Antioch City Council and had the honor to lead the Antioch School Board as President, helping guide decisions that affect our families and children’s future. More than 25 years in the financial industry, along with leadership across local government, made clear to me what residents need: sound planning, responsible budgeting, transparency that leads to results you can feel every day.

Beyond elected office, I remain deeply engaged in community service. I currently lead the Celebrate Antioch Foundation as President, serve as a Director on the Antioch Schools Education Foundation, as well as serving on the Chamber of Commerce, Antioch Women’s Club, and Antioch Historical Society. These roles reflect my commitment to strengthening partnerships and ensuring Antioch’s promise is fulfilled for every neighborhood.

If elected to the Antioch City Council, I will focus on four priorities: public safety, economic growth, community pride and accountability, and revitalizing downtown. I will advocate for data-driven public safety strategies; pursue policies that encourage investment and job creation; and promote city government that listens. I will address blight and vacant properties with consistent enforcement and replace neglect with opportunity. Finally, I will work to accelerate downtown revitalization, supporting increased commercial activity and walkable public spaces.
We can’t accept stagnancy. I will bring urgency, measurable goals, and accountability for a safer, stronger, more vibrant Antioch. Choose Joy!
As your District 1 Councilwoman, I’ve kept my promise to fight for working families, safer neighborhoods, and our most vulnerable residents.

I fought to bring more than $10 million in outside funding to the Department of Community Resources to support violence prevention and Antioch’s Youth Services Network—including the city’s S.O.A.R. internship program, which has already put 91 young adults facing real barriers into paid apprenticeships and a path toward a career.
I fought for $4 million in CalVIP grants to launch the Peace Fellowship, connecting residents at the center of gun violence with mentorship, wraparound resources, and accountability.

Because District 1 has felt the brunt of our homelessness crisis, I fought to secure a $34.9 million grant for permanent supportive housing—and I’ll continue pushing the city to invest in sustainable, long-term solutions to address our unhoused population.
I fought for renters, helping pass the Just Cause Eviction ordinance to stop unfair displacement by landlords.
I’ve called out vacant, blighted commercial properties that block economic development and fought to hold absentee landlords accountable.

Residents in the Sycamore area asked me for a long-term commitment to their safety. I fought harder than anyone on the council for the Sycamore Square police substation, bringing police and community resources to a neighborhood that has long been overlooked.
There’s more work ahead, and I’m not backing down. I’m asking for your vote, so I can keep fighting for an Antioch that works for all of us.
https://www.tamishaforantiochd1.com/

contests.title: City of Antioch, City Council, District 4

paragraphs: For more than 16 years, I have proudly called Antioch home, where I have built my career and dedicated myself to serving our community. As a business executive and Vice President of Human Resources for a multi-state healthcare organization, I oversee complex operations, strategic planning, labor relations, compliance, and workforce management for thousands of employees. Every day, I make thoughtful, accountable decisions that balance fiscal responsibility with the needs of people.

My commitment to public service extends beyond my profession. I have served as President of the Antioch Rotary Club, Chair of the Antioch Crime Prevention Commission, a member of the Antioch Unified School District Career Technical Education Committee, and a board member of the Antioch Public Schools Education Foundation and Delta Learning Center. These experiences have strengthened my commitment to collaboration, transparency, and delivering meaningful results for our community.

Antioch deserves leadership focused on practical solutions, accountability, and results. I will prioritize improving public safety, attracting new businesses and quality jobs, supporting youth and families, maintaining clean and safe neighborhoods, and ensuring responsible, compassionate solutions for our unhoused population. I believe we can strengthen our local economy, revitalize our commercial corridors, and make Antioch a destination where families and businesses choose to invest.

I am running for City Council because I believe Antioch’s greatest opportunities are still ahead. With proven executive leadership, community service, and a commitment to listening to and working with residents, I will bring integrity, experience, and a results-driven approach to City Hall.
Antioch has made real progress over the past several years—but our work isn’t done.
Economic Development

Creating jobs, attracting shopping and restaurants, and ensuring balanced growth are among my top priorities for District 4. I support responsible growth that brings jobs, housing, and the infrastructure our neighborhoods need to thrive. I also pushed for the city’s Just Cause Eviction ordinance and stronger protections against landlord retaliation.
Fiscal Responsibility

During two years of budget tightening, I fought to protect essential services while keeping Antioch’s finances on solid ground. When federal gridlock threatened city funding, I traveled to Washington to lobby federal agencies and elected officials to secure additional funding, including funds to address chronic flooding. I also fought for a dedicated grant writer because fiscal responsibility means competing for every tax dollar Antioch can get.
Clean Neighborhoods

Blighted, abandoned commercial properties hurt our community and local economy. I’ve fought to hold absentee commercial landlords accountable and put vacant buildings back into productive use. I also continue to support transitional housing and outreach programs helping move unhoused residents off our streets and into stable housing.

Great leaders listen. I’ve built my career by bringing people together, hearing their concerns, and solving problems collaboratively. As your District 4 councilwoman, I’ll continue to do so. I’m asking for your support so we can keep Antioch moving forward.
I am Matty Alappat and I am running for Antioch City Council, District 4, to help build a safer, cleaner and more prosperous community for all of us.
For the last 15 years I have worked in the software industry, solving tough problems and leading successful initiatives. I am ready to bring that same practical approach to City Council.

I was fortunate to be raised by a mom who was a science teacher and a dad who worked in banking. They taught me that success is built on hard work, integrity, respect for others, and giving back to your community — values I still live by today.
If elected, my top priority will be public safety. I will make sure the police have the resources required to fight crime and protect our neighborhoods.

We also have to take better care of our city. That means investing in city’s infrastructure, revitalizing downtown, maintaining clean pet-friendly public spaces and bringing in new businesses and good-paying jobs.

Housing policies must be carefully planned to fit existing neighborhoods and should only move forward where our infrastructure can truly support them. We will partner with nonprofits to help unhoused individuals achieve long-term stability and self-sufficiency, while also focusing on short-term transitional housing options.
Antioch deserves leadership that brings people together, spends taxpayer dollars wisely, and gets results. I am committed to making Antioch a place we can all be proud of.
I look forward to earning your support.

I’m running for Antioch City Council because I believe our city needs leaders who are willing to do the work–not just talk about it. Having been raised in Antioch and living here for 30 years, I have a connection to this community and knowledge of how our city has grown, changed, and the challenges we face today.

I have regularly attended City Council meetings, studied budgets, development proposals, infrastructure projects, and policy decisions. I have asked questions, listened to residents, and worked to offer solutions. Antioch deserves leadership that is engaged and accountable.

My priorities are restoring fiscal responsibility, strengthening public safety, growing Antioch’s economy, and attracting businesses that create local jobs. City government must live within its means, spend taxpayer dollars wisely, and make decisions that encourage investment rather than drive it away. A local economy creates opportunities for residents, improves city services, and builds a future.

As a District 4 resident and involved Antioch community member, I understand the importance of thoughtful planning, growth, and accountable government. City Hall should focus on solutions instead of political rhetoric. Every decision should be measured by one standard: does it improve the quality of life for Antioch residents?

I will continue listening to our community, making decisions based on facts, and ensuring taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly. My goal is to restore trust in local government, support economic growth, and build an Antioch where families and businesses can thrive.
I respectfully ask for your vote for Antioch City Council District 4.

paragraphs: For the past 10 years, I have proudly called Brentwood home. I’m running for City Council, District 2, because our community deserves leadership that listens, serves with integrity, and puts residents first. I believe leadership is about service and accountability to our community. I will listen, be transparent, and work collaboratively to find practical solutions. Together, we can preserve the values that make Brentwood a wonderful place to live while planning wisely for future generations. Learn more at tammyforbrentwood.com

Brentwood is a special place my three-generation family calls home – my parents, my wife and I, with four children in BUSD. I have been active in this community for several years, and I’m proud to serve as the Chairperson of Brentwood’s Planning Commission, fighting tirelessly to preserve the small-town community charm in alignment with our city’s General Plan.

I have been an active participant in shaping our community by serving on such committees as the Land Use and Development Committee, IME School Site Council, Measure B Oversight Committee, TRANSPLAN, and many more.

My Planning Commission votes speak for themselves; supporting projects like Costco, Streets of Brentwood building improvements, and the cap on gas stations, car washes, and drive-thrus. Maintaining a family-friendly environment and a focus on the future of Brentwood are at the heart of every decision I make.
Today’s leadership will have rippling effects for decades to come. Join me on this journey to amplify the origins of our great community. I’ll close with a quote:
“A society grows great when old men plant trees whose shade they know they shall never sit in.”
I would be honored to receive your vote.
Brandforbrentwood.com

I am running for Brentwood City Council, District 2, to bring my experience, community service, and practical problem-solving to City Hall. I am a 20-year Brentwood resident, married father of three, Senior Software Engineer, and community volunteer committed to serving our community.

My priorities are improving traffic, strengthening infrastructure, revitalizing Brentwood, protecting public safety, supporting local businesses, growing our local economy, and making sure growth is matched by the infrastructure and services our residents need.
I believe every resident deserves to be heard. I will communicate openly, work collaboratively, and focus on practical solutions that improve the quality of life for our families and neighborhoods.

I currently serve our community as a Brentwood Trustee with the Contra Costa Mosquito & Vector Control District, a Commissioner on the Contra Costa County Airport Land Use Commission, a School Site Council Parent Member, and in other local community leadership roles.

Through these roles, I have worked with people from many backgrounds on issues involving public health, neighborhoods, schools, transportation, land use, and community priorities. These experiences have taught me the importance of teamwork, practical solutions, and responsible use of limited resources.
After 20 years of calling Brentwood home, I would be honored to continue serving our community on the City Council and to serve the residents of District 2 and all of Brentwood.
I respectfully ask for your vote on November 3, 2026.

paragraphs: The decisions we make today will shape our neighborhoods, local economy, infrastructure, and quality of life for years to come. I’m running for Brentwood City Council because I want to help strengthen our community while preparing Brentwood for the future.

I also served as Chair of the Brentwood Parks & Recreation Commission, where I championed inclusive recreation and accessibility for residents of all abilities.

My husband and I are the co-founders of Miles for Mayo, a nonprofit that hosts an annual 5K at Veterans Park, bringing hundreds of people of all ages together to promote movement, build community, and strengthen the connections that make Brentwood special.

Throughout my career and public service, I’ve learned the best decisions come from listening, evaluating the facts, and considering different perspectives. That’s the approach I’ll bring to the Brentwood City Council. I’ll come prepared, respect different viewpoints, and make thoughtful decisions that strengthen our community.
I would be honored to receive your vote for Brentwood City Council.
www.stephanieforbrentwood.com

My name is Sheree Shannon, and I am running for City Council, District 4. As a proud Brentwood resident for 23 years, a mom of three, and a grandmother of four, I’ve managed my husband’s remodeling business for 36 years while also serving as a Realtor, author, and co-founder of Rise Up, inspiring women to pursue their purpose.

Leading by example, I am pursuing my purpose to positively impact our city as I partner with the Mayor and City Council to create an environment where every resident can thrive while feeling safe and connected.
Public safety is non-negotiable. When tragedy strikes, response time matters. We must ensure our emergency services are fully staffed and have what they need to keep us safe.

Smart city planning requires strong infrastructure while protecting the character of our existing neighborhoods. We need responsible growth that strengthens our local economy, expands housing opportunities, provides quality jobs, and preserves the Brentwood we love. Moving Brentwood forward will take fiscal responsibility, integrity, and strategic planning, and I am prepared to bring those qualities.

My experience managing a successful business for 36 years through economic downturns, changing markets, and the pandemic has prepared me to make sound decisions, solve complex problems, and lead with confidence. I will bring that same proven leadership and practical experience to serving Brentwood.
With dedication, laser focus, and hard work, Brentwood will remain strong, safe, and a place we are all proud to call home. I respectfully ask for your vote.
My name is Holley Bishop-Mello, and I am asking for your vote for Brentwood City Council District 4.

I was born and raised in Brentwood and am a proud mother, Human Resources professional, and small business owner. For more than 25 years, I helped organizations solve problems, build consensus, and serve people. Today, I work in agriculture and understand firsthand the challenges facing local businesses, working families, and our farming community.

My involvement in our community comes from a simple belief: the people of Brentwood deserve to be heard. I have stood alongside residents, small business owners, families, and city employees to advocate for the issues that affect their everyday lives.

I have advocated for fair wages for city employees and emergency responders, safe drinking water, and greater parental involvement and transparency in our schools. When residents felt their voices weren’t being heard, I stood with them and spoke up. That experience strengthened my belief that elected officials have a responsibility to listen – even when they disagree.

As your Council member, I will support public safety, responsible growth, small businesses, agriculture, and fiscal responsibility. I will work to protect Brentwood’s quality of life while considering the financial impact local government decisions have on our residents and businesses. I will ask questions, listen to residents, and make decisions based on what is best for our community.
Brentwood’s future should be shaped by the people who live here – not outside interests.
It would be an honor to earn your vote.

As a nurse and healthcare leader, I have held management, supervisory, pediatric special-needs, and care-management positions, earning recognition from Today’s Nurse for my advocacy and leadership in patient care. Additionally, I serve on the Clayton Community Library Foundation Board and volunteer at events such as Clayton Cleans Up, the Art & Wine Festival, the Fourth of July parade, and Oktoberfest.

I bring extensive experience in managing budgets, ensuring regulatory compliance, and being accountable for my decisions. I am not a political insider; I am committed to working on behalf of all Clayton residents.

My decision to run for office is inspired by the need to address significant challenges facing Clayton, including a limited budget, state housing mandates, aging infrastructure, fire safety, and ensuring residents have a seat at the table.

I have been a proud Clayton resident and homeowner since 2002, raising two children here, alongside my husband, Chris. With a degree in Business Management, I am a Senior Commercial Property Manager with 30 years’ experience working with large property and facility budgets, project management, planning, and property development and redevelopment. I have extensive experience working with city governments and local agencies throughout the Bay Area. I write, review, and operate contracts every day while mentoring a large staff and many vendors. My work helps to grow companies and property portfolios. I would be honored to have your vote.

paragraphs: My name is Robyn Kuslits, and I’m running to be your District 3 representative for Concord’s City Council.

I’m running because I believe our community deserves a local government that stands up for their safety, listens to their concerns, and fights for their needs. District 3 is the gateway to Concord, and the amount of traffic and commerce throughout our district must be adequately met with quality roads, pedestrian safety measures, and economic development. I’ll advocate for these issues as I did with city staff, leading to installation of 3 crosswalks across busy Market/Meadow Streets. Our district is unique as home to tenants, homeowners, the Community Youth Center, and commercial business areas. Join me in uplifting these people and spaces by connecting one to the other with safe roads, thriving properties, and community hubs we can create. I’ll take my experience identifying resources for families and strive to provide more where need exists – especially for women & children, tenants, small business, the elderly, and the disenfranchised. I volunteer at school and in our community, support my firefighter husband’s demanding career, and am raising our children with bilingual education and community involvement. I’ve been active on our County Commission for Women & Girls and Measure X Community Advisory Board. My skills are unique to the council, but not to those of us doing the work in our neighborhoods to make Concord better for our families. I’d be honored to have your vote for City Council.
https://www.instagram.com/denaabcommunity/
Concord gave my family a place to build a future, and I am running for City Council to make sure more families have that same opportunity.

I came to the United States from Peru with determination, a work ethic, and the belief that service to others matters. Today, I am a husband, father, small business owner, and healthcare leader who is proud to call District 3 home.

As Founder and CEO of Empower Minds ABA, I work with children with autism and their families throughout Contra Costa County. That experience has shown me how important it is for leaders to listen, respond with compassion, and turn concerns into action.

I believe in keeping our residents safe. We deserve timely emergency response and neighborhoods where people feel secure. Our current crisis preparedness is uncertain, and that must change. We also urgently need to improve street safety, especially along the Monument corridor.

My direct public-sector experience comes from senior leadership roles inside a public agency, where I led a team that saved over $100 million over five years with no layoffs. I will continue working to keep our police and fire departments staffed and accountable; repair our streets, sidewalks, and storm drains; welcome new businesses to grow our tax base; and maintain and expand programs for youth and seniors.

I’m Mary Ann (MJ) Jawili, and I’m running for El Cerrito City Council.

I’ve been a resident and homeowner in El Cerrito for 18 years, and I love this city. But in all the time I’ve lived here, I’ve never seen an election as polarized as our last primary. People feel they’re not being listened to, and they’ve turned away from their city and their community as a result.

Community is what I do. From hosting dinners with friends to serving as president of an 850-member cycling club, I work to bring people together. Our city deserves leadership that listens first, cares deeply, and acts with integrity. As a city councillor I’ll listen with empathy, especially to residents who feel unheard. I’ll proactively meet residents where they are and communicate in plain language. I’ll bring transparency to how decisions are made and how money is spent. I’ll keep community at the center of policy because a city’s greatness is measured by how well it serves its residents.
El Cerrito doesn’t need more division. It needs someone who will do the necessary work to bring us back together, and that’s what I’m committed to doing.

Forrest Lanning is a Bay Area native, structural engineer, and neighbor. He earned a degree in Architectural Engineering from California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly) and later conducted earthquake engineering research at Stanford University. A career spanning more than two decades, Forrest has dedicated his work to helping communities become safer and more resilient through practical problem-solving, and responsible stewardship of public resources.

Forrest lived and worked overseas, helping communities recover from major earthquakes and tsunamis in New Zealand, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan, Costa Rica, and Colombia. Working with organizations including USAID, the United Nations, the World Bank, and local governments, he led disaster recovery programs that rebuilt and retrofitted schools, strengthened critical infrastructure, and improved earthquake preparedness. Managing projects with limited budgets taught him the importance of prioritizing investments, eliminating waste, and finding practical solutions that deliver the greatest benefit for every dollar spent. These experiences reinforced his belief that effective leadership begins with listening to the community, evaluating the facts, and making thoughtful, practical decisions that put residents first.

Forrest and his wife, Sara, are proud to call El Cerrito home. He is committed to serving the community with integrity, common sense, and sound judgment, working collaboratively to solve problems and make thoughtful decisions that reflect the best interests of both today’s residents and future generations.
I’m a new father, a homeowner, and an experienced business leader. I’m running for City Council because I believe we need to change the status quo in El Cerrito.

If elected, I won’t spend my time on junkets or networking for higher office. I’m running to serve El Cerrito: to make sure the city listens to residents, to provide real oversight, and to invest in our quality of life.
I’m someone who digs into the details and asks hard questions when something doesn’t add up.

I helped lead the opposition to the proposed library tax. We read the fine print and flagged its problems, from the ballooning price tag to a senior exemption almost no senior could qualify for. Voters agreed, defeating it by a 70 to 30 margin.

My wife and I bought our first home in El Cerrito in 2023 and are raising our newborn daughter Margot here. I run the consumer team at Impulse Labs, a San Francisco electronics company. Earlier, I helped grow a startup to 140 employees with no outside investment. We competed against Walmart and Costco, so wasting money wasn’t an option.
On the Council, I will bring that discipline to our budget, demand transparency in how decisions get made, and listen to neighbors before the city makes plans, not after.
You won’t always agree with me, but I’m happy to meet with anyone and will always be honest about what’s going on and why.
I hope to earn your vote.

Improving our public safety through maintaining fast emergency medical response times and increasing wildfire prevention efforts and community policing.

Protecting taxpayers by responsibly managing city finances leading S&P to raise our bond rating to A+, saying that they‘ ve seen “ a continued improvement in (our) financial position and enhanced financial management policies and practices.”
Protecting our environment by supporting laws on the Bay Area Air District board to reduce air pollution and city policies to Increase recycling and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Supporting policies making our streets safer and more walkable.
Promoting equity by supporting affordable housing near transit as recognized by Governor Newsom declaring us an official Prohousing Community.
I’m working to grow our revenues and tax base to build a sustainable future for our residents and small businesses, and ensure public safety, recreation and senior services meet our residents’ needs.

I work with our Federal, State and County representatives to deliver results for El Cerrito, and I’ve earned endorsements from Congressmember John Garamendi, State Senator Jesse Arreguin, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, Supervisor John Gioia, and many neighborhood leaders. I am running for Hercules City Council to bring transparent and accountable leadership to our city government. While we’ve accomplished a great deal, our work is not finished. I remain committed to enhancing public safety, completing the revitalization of our marina and waterfront, supporting local businesses, improving infrastructure, addressing homelessness through regional partnerships, and ensuring Martinez remains a safe, welcoming, and financially strong community. I look forward to continuing to work alongside residents to preserve what makes Martinez special while thoughtfully planning for the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead.

My name is Nakenya, and I am running for Martinez City Council District 1 because I believe our city is full of promise—and that with thoughtful leadership, and community-centered decision-making, we can see the progress we have been waiting for.

As a long-time resident and parent raising a child with special needs, I understand firsthand how city decisions affect families, neighborhoods, services, safety, accessibility, and quality of life. My experience has taught me to analyze, advocate persistently, and work through challenges with patience, compassion, and determination.

I have followed local decisions and engaged with the issues that shape our future. That involvement has strengthened my belief that effective governance must be transparent, accountable, inclusive, and responsive to the people it serves.

As your Councilmember, I will work to support responsible growth, strengthen public safety, improve accessibility for residents of all abilities, and ensure that major decisions are made with meaningful community input. Our city deserves a foundation that is practical, fair, financially responsible, and focused on long-term results.

Leadership is about showing up, listening, bringing people together, all while making decisions with integrity. I will be a voice for families, working residents, seniors, small businesses, people with disabilities, and every neighbor who wants to see our city thrive.

District 1 needs leadership that is accessible, engaged, and committed to building a stronger future for all of us. I am ready to serve, and to help bring out the full potential of our city. I respectfully ask for your support.
